text: Hello everyone and welcome to another
video. My track guide for the BMW M2 CSR
going around Summit Point, the Jefferson
layout. Let's get into it. Turn one is a
place where people will try and overtake
you in the race. But when qualifying be
on the left side of the track once I
start to lose the wall here on the left,
I start to break and I aim for about 90%
brake pressure, trailing that off all
the way to the top of the corner,
hitting as close as we can to the inside
curb without hitting it. You can use
third here, but I use second. I feel I
get a bit more acceleration out of it.
Because I'm using second, I need to be a
little bit more smooth with the throttle
inputs. Once we start to go a little bit
up the hill, we start to accelerate
again. We need to be really smooth with
the throttle application. Then we want
to cut the first inside curb of turn
two. And as we cross the middle of the
track, we want to break a little bit, no
more than 10%, cutting the second curb
as well, ending up in the middle of the
track for turn three. I don't have a
clear good braking marker for turn
three, but this is just about where I
start to break. Here I aim for about 50%
brake pressure, and we are trailing that
off all the way to the top of the
corner. Here, I prefer to stay close to
the inside curb. Just before the corner
turns a little bit more, we start to
accelerate again. And we are easing in
the throttle, short shifting as well
into third, making sure we're not going
wider than the middle of the track. Then
it's all about balance and making sure
you stay close to the inside curb. Turn
four as well. Stay as far to the right
side of the track as you dare. I break
once I lose the tree here on the left. I
aim for about 80% brake pressure,
trailing that off all the way to the
inside curb. I prefer to not hit the
curb as I feel that makes the car quite
unstable. Once we get to the inside
curb, we want to slowly start to apply
the throttle again. It's really easy to
hit the traction control here and lose
momentum. Make sure you don't go onto
the grass because that will spin the
car. If you get a bad exit out of turn
five, people will try and overtake you
into turn six. But when qualifying, you
want to be as far right as possible. For
turn six, my braking marker is the end
of the curb here on the right. I aim for
about 70% brake pressure, and we're
easing off the pressure all the way to
the top of the little hill before turn.
I prefer to take a tighter line here
getting close into the inside curb of
turn six. And then I aim for just about
mid track before turn seven. As we get
to the top of the hill, we want to have
the car turn and we want to start to
accelerate again. And of course, we want
to get as close as we can to the inside
curb. And we want to be smooth with the
throttle because it's really easy to
spin the car. And of course, we use all
of the room we need on the outside.
